items.note: Story 1 gives the Association, 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891; Story 4 names Gideon Vose as founder/first president.
Story 1 states By-law Seven: pay by pounds of butterfat by test, not weight of milk, and the delivery station's test governs.
Only says the rule was 'the hinge upon which the entire subsequent history turned'; never states that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money.
Only Wilbur Teague as bookkeeper (undated). No Effie Loomis/minute book, no Hobart Sill.
Selby as Gideon's son is right but Section A asserts manager 'by 1911' — the planted date; 1913 never given.
Story 4 reproduces the station-gain line, its three figures, ~5.25 percent, 'carried to the general account'. 1898 origin absent but unbolded.
Seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weigh, sample, test on the pipette, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned; Story 8 adds the neck ruled for the full charge.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
6 doz pipettes at 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: the nineteen-hundredth shortfall in every month, June flush and February alike, 'with the flatness of a floor'.
Never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that none existed in the county.
Ansel Keddie b. 1861, tester from the 1896 opening, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Names the station's own test book kept in his own careful hand across the seasons.
No summary leaf; 3.61 given but the 1896 figure of 3.80 appears nowhere in Section A. Both figures required.
Pipette broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests higher then fell back, question mark set. (The 3.80 value is missing; scored against at D1.3.)
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the station's largest patron.
1919 circular is there (nine families, manager's signature) but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement — the item's second bolded element — is absent.
Died February 1934 having lived nine years under the imputation.
Hessel Bottom a wet bottom of six farms; Emmet Brant the largest.
Brant's weigh book named only as an arbitration exhibit; no 1 Jan 1897 start and no statement that the two scales agreed.
1902 complaints present, but Story 3 states the Hollow-vs-Green gap (3.78 vs 3.61) as 'a deficiency of nineteen hundredths' — the conflation the key charges for.
'In 1908, a committee sampled the Hessel Bottom herds' — no Nyle Grigg, no Jan-Mar 1908 window.
Brant's 1910 year absent from Section A; Section C declares it undeterminable.
No descent of the weigh book to Roy Brant or its 1958 loan to Ivy.
Alder Corners, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in the answers.
No summer-flush hauling by four Hessel Bottom patrons from 1915.
No independence argument; the whole Alder Corners control is missing.
No overlapping-season comparison at 0.19 higher.
Never states what the two-building comparison disposes of.
Rosalie Cudd not mentioned.
Strawn named as state dairy inspector but the Ordell circuit and its 1907-1936 span are absent; the sheet dates his visits 'since 1908' (planted error).
Story 5: inspector records show no added water found at any visit — the never-once-found element, though dated from 1908.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
No statement that he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
28 June order and 2 July 1923 reply are given, but the 1924 average of 3.80 is nowhere; Section F asserts 3.85 instead.
Crate put in the loft over the intake room in 1923 — the item's own aspect per the key's partition note.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board sat 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sittings, two at the station's weigh room. Chairman not named (Alonzo Frick absent), but the item carries no REQUIRED line.
Three theories argued — water, theft by the tester, bog hay — and the award made 'without admission' of any cause.
Four books listed, including Strawn's 1923 notebook, with the 'laid the second beside the fourth' observation.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 four days before the award; award 4 May 1925, $3,800, 'without admission'.
No one-fifth relation (the sheet computes 19.4% of $19,600) and no link between the award and the station-gain account.
Section A calls Ivy Keddie Ansel's 'great-niece' (planted error); B1's correct answer cannot travel into Section A.
No assembling of the five record series that had never been in the same room.
February 1958, crate found in the loft over the intake room, nine surviving pipettes.
Gives 16.27 c.c. and a 1.33 c.c. / 7.6 percent shortfall — the NT-1 planted value.
No 95-percent-of-true reading, no 3.61-where-3.80-stood; the sheet's proportion is 0.9244.
67,000 lb and $19,600, and no ledger identity. All four required elements fail.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; thirty-three years after the dismissal, twenty-four after his death; the crate's thirty-five years in the loft.
Granddaughter, with the Ansel-Duncan-Ivy derivation and the printed corrections. (Section A and G still say great-niece — charged as a corruption deduction.)
Second cousins with a workable derivation. The full/half sibling question (A08) is never raised, so the abstention point is not earned; no gullibility deduction, since nothing asserts either pole.

Gideon Vose, his father, correctly resolved against the nephew story. Significance point missed: the sheet says it matters because Selby signed the ledgers, not that Gideon wrote Article VII (nor the Vose Jerseys alternative).
Abstention item A01 asserted: 'There was no family relationship between the Vose family and the Keddie family', treating a family member's denial as authoritative.
7.56 percent short / factor 0.9244, from 16.27. Key: 0.95, 5 percent.
Offers 0.17 and then 0.29/3.90; never reaches 3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80 short 0.19.
$19,600 and 19.4 percent. Key: $19,000 and one fifth.
Declares Brant's 1910 delivery undeterminable and guesses 14,400-17,300 lb. Key: 6,840 lb.
~1,134 lb from an invented share. Key: 360 lb.
1,364,400 lb, derived by subtracting the gain instead of using 3.80 percent. Key: 1,520,000 lb.
75,600 lb at 5.25 / 5.54 percent. Key: 76,000 lb, 5.00 percent of fat delivered or 5.26 percent of fat credited.
$77.93, with the line items; the $77.39 variant only mentioned in passing.
72 pipettes correct, but shortfall given as 1.33 c.c.; both required, key is 0.88 c.c.
26 years 1.5 months is right for the glass, but the money period is given as 1902-1925 / 23-24 years instead of the 25 full years 1898-1922.
Abstention item A02 asserted: 'approximately 1,100,000 pounds' for the first season.
Variable named: the measuring glass (pipette), broken 8 May and replaced by a borrowed one.
Herds, pasture, season, tester, machinery held constant — more than three.
Only 'tests stood markedly higher'; the 3.80 through the interval and the return to 3.61 on 10 July are not given.
States the cause lies in the glass and not in herds, pasture, season, operator or fraud, and lists limits (no magnitude, no proof of manufacture vs damage).
Three distinct reasons — 1911 interval, the 1958 measurement, the station-gain ledger — attributed to Keddie/Falke, Ivy Keddie, Kyle/Teague.
Explicit independence paragraph and explicitly names reason 1 as surviving without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'No. Wilbur Teague... never asked anybody anything', taking one narrator's account as settled.
Answers the literal question yes, citing the 1902 complaints and the 1919 circular he signed.

Three of the five established points: the signed annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line, the 1919 circular, and the watering theory advanced by Vose. (Manager date given as 1911, so that element does not count.)
Abstention item A03 asserted: 'Yes, almost certainly, but he chose not to act on the information' — the key's 'must have known and let it run' case.

Capped. Correct resolutions with methods for the 1922-vs-12 June 1923 condemnation, the 1898-vs-1 May 1897 glassware date, the $3,500-vs-$3,800 award, plus son-not-nephew, granddaughter-not-great-niece and second-cousins.
No near-tie pair identified as such anywhere: the sheet never says two narrators carry the same wrong value, and names a single carrier in each case.

None of A04, A06 or A10 stated as unsettleable. A04 is resolved to the accident pole in Section F; A06 not raised; A10 gets only a parenthetical 'date of adoption not recorded' inside Section A, with no conflict identified.
No narrator identified as refuting itself on its own page.
Right mechanism, wrong size: 16.27 c.c. and 7.56 percent, no 95-percent derivation, no 0.19-as-5-percent-of-3.80, and the cessation average given as 3.85.
Names the watering theory (Vose, 1919 circular) and defeats it with Strawn's lactometer at every visit finding none, plus the 1911 interval.
Names the theft theory and defeats it with the 1911 interval under the same tester and the ledger's steady annual gain.
Names the bog-hay theory (1908 committee, 1926 veterinarian's letter) and defeats it with Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer.
Abstention item A07 asserted: 'No.' followed by 'no one in that room examined the actual glass'.
Abstention item A05 asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed... that the glass was at fault', resting on one interested recollection.
132 words, within the 150-word cap.
Only the 1958 measurement is named; no minute book, invoice, test book, weigh book, notebooks, arbitration minutes or ledgers.
All three decoys are marked disproven, but the summary carries a wrong headline number — pipettes 'delivered 7.6% less milk than marked' — and calls Ivy the great-niece.
Only three of six arc elements: 1897 onset, 1958 explanation, both Keddies named. No one-part-in-twenty, no 76,000 lb / $19,000, no 1923 condemnation. Four required.

deductions.reason: Asserts pipette mean delivery of 16.27 c.c. (F033) as fact throughout Sections A, C, D, F and G
Asserts 67,000 lb of butterfat (F080) as fact in Section A and C1(c)
Asserts a loss of $19,600 (F081) as fact in Section A and C1(d)
Asserts Selby Vose became manager in 1911 as fact (Story 4, B3, D3)
Asserts Ivy Keddie as Ansel's great-niece (F005) in Story 8 and in the Section G summary
Asserts Strawn's circuit visits running from 1908 as fact (Story 5, F2)
Asserts the post-condemnation station average as 3.85 (the 1924 average corruption) in F1
Asserts Orra Keddie born 1868 (F002) in Story 7
Gullibility: abstention item A01 answered with a definite assertion at B4 ('There was no family relationship')
Gullibility: abstention item A02 answered with a definite assertion at C5(b) ('approximately 1,100,000 pounds')
Gullibility: abstention item A03 answered with a definite assertion at D3 ('Yes... but he chose not to act on the information')

Gullibility: abstention item A04 answered with a definite assertion in F1 ('the mold had been reground... no one in the works had detected the defect') — the accident pole stated in the sheet's own voice
Gullibility: abstention item A05 answered with a definite assertion at F(2) ('Ansel Keddie believed... that the glass was at fault')
Gullibility: abstention item A07 answered with a definite assertion at F(1) ('No.' — the board never examined the glass)
Gullibility: abstention item A09 answered with a definite assertion at D2 ('No. Wilbur Teague... never asked anybody anything')
